question: Can unconsumed interactive rollout groups be repaired after policy and feedback-verifier changes while preserving the current target group law at lower total collection cost?
phase: Prerequisite falsification, not a model-learning or efficiency experiment
scope: Three analytically specified finite-law checks plus imported pinned SPEC-RL acceptance kernel. No pretrained model, retired cohort, GPU or API inference.

methods: accept min(1,p/q), reject then sample p
accept min(1,p/q), reject then sample normalized (p-q)+
cases.metric: exact output law and group-size-two normalized expected score update

cases.target_selection: p(action1)=0.9 if first consumed draft action=1, else 0.1
methods: correct residual kernel using consumed draft
correct residual kernel using independent unconsumed donor group
cases.metric: conditional group law TV and expected group-normalized score update

cases.policy: first action1 probability .5; second action1 probability .2 after feedback0 and .9 after feedback1
methods: replay feedback, regenerate at first changed observation
cases.metric: exact trajectory law TV, expected reward, count of regenerated action calls

sampling_sanity.purpose: execute pinned spec_cut only; target continuation simulated, no Ray/vLLM end-to-end claim

pass_conditions: fresh independent donor with correct residual matches target group law to 1e-12
first-feedback-change repair matches fresh trajectory law to 1e-12
consumed-draft exactness counterexample has conditional TV > .05
published-style rejection has exact TV > .05 and imported acceptance kernel empirical law agrees within .005
stop_conditions: Any independent-donor or feedback-repair exactness check fails: stop implementation
Do not start training from finite-law success alone
No new synthetic variants after these checks
Do not claim novel speculative sampling or off-dynamics theory; novelty of joint systems contribution remains provisional
